options.label: Reduce reservoir capacity and convert catchment land to high-density housing, relying on NEWater to supply all shortfalls.
Link multiple catchment areas into a shared reservoir network with expanded storage, and coordinate reservoir levels with NEWater and desalination outputs to buffer dry spells.
Prioritise importing more water during dry spells and treat reservoirs only as emergency backup, with no changes to catchment capture.
Replace most reservoirs with desalination plants so the system no longer depends on rainfall variability.

candidates.stem: You are advising a water utility on an integrated strategy to strengthen Singapore’s local catchment reservoirs against extended dry weather while still capturing stormwater during intense rain. Which proposal best synthesises the reservoirs’ role within the Four National Taps?

options.label: Allow development right up to the reservoir edge with no treatment, since the reservoir’s treatment plant can remove all contaminants.
Install vegetated swales, rain gardens, and detention basins to slow and treat runoff before it reaches the reservoir, while preserving a vegetated buffer around the water body.
Line all drains and channels with concrete to speed runoff directly into the reservoir, maximising inflow volume.
Divert all stormwater away from the reservoir to a separate drain, so the new district has zero impact on reservoir water.

candidates.stem: A new residential district is planned inside a water catchment that drains into a local reservoir. Which integrated design best sustains both reservoir yield and raw water quality for Singapore’s local catchment tap?

proposed_test_set.description: This test set assesses synthesis-level understanding of reservoirs as one of Singapore's Four National Taps within the local catchment. Learners evaluate integrated proposals for sustaining reservoir yield and water quality.
proposed_test_set.title: Reservoirs: Synthesis Assessment for Singapore's Local Catchment
